STEP_ALL.doc: Sentinel for backup_step's n_pages parameter meaning 'copy every remaining page in this call'. Mainline parity with sqlite3_backup_step's nPage = -1. Targets render the constant in their idiomatic form (Rust pub const, C #define, Go const, Zig pub const, Python module-level).

BackupHandle.doc: Public handle returned by backup_init and consumed by step / finish / remaining / pagecount. Wraps a BackupEngine plus the abstract obligation to keep the source and destination Database references alive for the handle's lifetime. Targets render the two borrows idiomatically (Rust holds &Database, C holds raw handle pointers, Python holds object references). The handle MUST NOT outlive either Database; spec-side this is an obligation, not a checkable invariant.

BackupStepResult.doc: Outcome of a single backup_step. Ok means more pages remain to be copied (or the call was a no-op for n_pages=0); the caller MAY issue another step. Done means every page has been copied AND the destination commit has been finalized; the caller's next call must be finish. Error wraps a RuntimeCondition; whether the error is recoverable (caller retries step) or terminal (caller proceeds to finish) is determined by the condition's classification.

Ok.doc: Progress was made (or n_pages was 0); more pages remain or a restart was triggered.

Done.doc: Every page copied; destination committed; caller proceeds to finish.

Error.doc: The step failed; condition classifies whether retry is admissible.

BackupInitError.doc: Failure modes of backup_init. SameDatabase is raised when source and destination resolve to the same (Database, schema-name) pair (Pin B1). UnknownSchema is raised when either schema name does not resolve in its respective Database. PageSizeMismatch is raised when the destination already contains a database with a page size differing from the source's (Pin B7). EngineOpen wraps a lower-level lock-acquisition failure surfaced by the storage layer.

SameDatabase.doc: src and dst resolve to the same (Database, schema-name) pair.

UnknownSchema.doc: side is 'src' or 'dst'; schema_name is the unresolved name.

BackupFinishError.doc: Failure modes of backup_finish. v1 admits no failure cases at the spec layer (see master.md §Algorithm); the variant exists so targets that surface a target-specific I/O failure during dst rollback have a place to put it. Targets that have nothing to report MAY render finish as returning unit instead of Result<unit, BackupFinishError>.

RollbackIo.doc: An I/O condition fired while rolling back the destination.

backup_init.doc: Open a backup handle copying the schema named src_name within src_db into the schema named dst_name within dst_db. v1 admits 'main' for both names; other names are admitted by the shape and resolved by the storage layer. Pin B1 forbids backup-to-self. Pin B7 fixes the page-size handshake. After init, pagecount(handle) reflects the source's page count and remaining(handle) equals pagecount(handle) (Pin B10).

backup_step.doc: Copy up to n_pages source pages into the destination. n_pages == STEP_ALL means 'every remaining page in this call'. n_pages == 0 is a no-op (Pin B12). Returns Ok if more pages remain, Done if the backup is complete, Error(condition) on a per-page or per-snapshot failure. Restart-on-source-write (Pin B4) is signalled by the public accessors (pagecount/remaining), NOT by an Error variant.

backup_finish.doc: Release the handle. If the engine state is Completed (the most recent step returned Done), this releases storage handles and locks. Otherwise, the destination is rolled back to its pre-init state and locks are released. Idempotent: calling finish on an already-finished handle is a no-op (Pin B9). Targets MAY render finish as consuming the handle (Rust's by-value); the spec admits both consuming and non-consuming renderings.

backup_remaining.doc: Pages in the source that have not yet been copied in the current pass. Decreases monotonically as step makes progress within a pass; on a Pin B4 restart, jumps back up to the new pagecount. Valid immediately after init (Pin B10). O(1) read.

backup_pagecount.doc: Total pages in the source as of the most recently observed source snapshot. Refreshed at every step entry that observes a source-write since the prior observation (Pin B4). Valid immediately after init (Pin B10). O(1) read.
